Petitioner has filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., whereby it is prayed that the
impugned order dated 15.2.2021 passed by the 20th Asj, Indore in Crr No.26679/2020 be
modified suitably b
y deleting the Para No.12 of the impugned order.
Brief facts of the case are that applicant is a private limited company.

Accused Abhimanyu Sharma has obtained the financial assistance of Rs.2,08,50,000/- from Bajaj Finance Limited and mortgaged his several properties with them by depositing the title documents and sale deed with
Bajaj Finance Ltd.
The aforesaid loan has been assigned to the applicant-Company by Bajaj Finance Ltd. vide deed of assignment dated 29.12.2017.
Police has registered Crime No.69/2018 against the accused Abhimanyu Sharma for the offence under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC and sent a letter to the applicant on 4.4.2018.
Police seized the original title documents, sale deeds and loan agreement from the applicant company by seizure memo dated 26.4.2018.
Applicant has initiated the recovery proceedings against the accused Abhimanyu Sharma and other accused persons.
Applicant has filed an application under Section 451 & 457 of Cr.P.C. for obtaining the seized original documents on Supurdgi.
Vide order dated 21.10.2019 the trial Court has dismissed their application.

Thereafter applicant has preferred Criminal Revision before this Court and the same was finally disposed of by the High Court with a direction to the trial Court to hear the matter again on merit, but the trial Court has again dismissed his application vide order dated 6.10.2020.

Then petitioner 10:41:19 AM has preferred a Revision before the revisional court and by order dated 15.2.2021 same was allowed, but the court has imposed a condition of execution of bond of Rs.1 Crore to submit the documents whenever the court will require the said documents.
Being aggrieved by the imposition of the condition of bond of Rs.1 Crore, the petitioner has filed this petition.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the impugned order dated 15.2.2021 is contrary to the law and facts on record.
The documents seized from the applicant are genuine.
Applicant company is a financial institution and the money of the company is also public money.
Applicant is suffering huge loss of public money due to the non availability of original mortgage documents and recovery of the aforesaid amount is also pending since long.
Applicant has no relation with the offence committed by the accused persons.
Hence he prays that the impugned order be modified by deleting the Para-12 ofthe impugned order.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection.
He has informed that as per the order of the DIG (Police), foreclosure report has been submitted before the trial Court.

sentences.text: 2 After due consideration, it does appear that applicant-Company is not the accused in the aforesaid offence.
Only agreement executed by the accused Abhimanyu Sharma in favour of the complainant Ajay Sharma is disputed.
Concerned documents have been recovered from the possession of the present applicant.
Applicant is not an accused and has not considered to be involved in any conspiracy with other co-accused persons.
Hence, imposition of such erroneous condition would be improper.

From the perusal of the impugned order, it appears that the learned trial Court has not given any reason, even obliquely, which has been compelled him to seek a bond of Rs.1 Crore from the applicant while giving the seized documents on interim custody to him.
Having regard to the aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that no such bond is required for giving the seized document on interim custody to the applicant.
Therefore, the part of the impugned order dated 15.2.2021 directing the applicant to submit a bond of Rs.1 Crore is entirely arbitrary and dictorial.

For the aforesaid analysis, this M.Cr.C. is allowed and the part of the impugned order dated 15.2.2021, whereby the learned revisional court has sought the bond of Rs.1 Crore against the interim custody of the seized document, is deleted and instead thereof the applicant shall submit a solvent surety of an amount of Rs.10 Lakhs to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
It is made clear that the remaining part of the impugned order shall remain intact.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. is finally disposed of.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned trial Court for necessary compliance.
C.C. as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE trilok Phoenix Arc Private Ltd. Acting As A ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110427822/
